direction.reason: Reduced moderate to slight weakening. Weak factory orders and the official China contraction still limit demand, but the private China PMI beat, hotter inflation gauge and approvals rebound materially offset the earlier external-shock argument. Domestic capacity and core-price persistence support restraint; a likely November hike is baseline, not proof of a longer sequence. The external-demand constraint narrowly dominates before the RBA. A stronger multi-meeting policy path or broader demand recovery would defeat weakness. AUD has firmer domestic policy support than NZD.

evidence.title: Australia service and construction costs persist despite fuel relief
evidence.facts: ABS final-demand PPI rose 1.1% q/q and 3.6% y/y, after 1.3% and 3.6%. Construction and services drove increases; skilled-labour constraints and scheduled wage/indexation adjustments mattered. Building output rose 1.3%, manufacturing output fell 1.3%, mainly petroleum/coal. Lower fuel prices partly offset freight and labour pressure. PPI is producer pricing, not consumer core inflation, and these components are one package.

evidence.title: Australia CPI and RBA capacity reassessment
evidence.facts: ABS September headline CPI is 4.3% y/y versus 4.0% in August; monthly-series trimmed mean is 3.6% versus revised 3.5%. The RBA says labour conditions look tighter than previously judged despite higher unemployment, productivity is weak and domestic/international upside inflation risks have materialised. NAB shifted to a November 25 bp hike forecast. It reports quarterly trimmed mean 1.0% q/q and 3.7% y/y against attributed consensus 1.0%/3.6%. Monthly core was broadly expected; monthly and quarterly core series differ and are not competing actuals. No RBA November promise was made. In the same October 28 note, NAB expects a November hike to 4.85%, then a likely pause, describing policy as restrictive. It says the marginal September core reading was broadly expected and did not further fuel concern about more persistent components. This limits the inference from a likely near-term hike to a continuing sequence; it is an institutional forecast rather than RBA forward guidance.
evidence.timing_note: Original source date retained. Publication/update hour not independently established; verification does not redate the release.

evidence.title: Australia trade prices: import-cost relief alongside higher export prices
evidence.facts: ABS September-quarter export prices rose 1.4% q/q and 6.3% y/y; import prices fell 1.1% q/q and rose 5.5% y/y. Export gains included gas +28.6%, coal +4.8% and cereals +5.7%, opposed by ores -6.4% and non-monetary gold -4.8%. Import declines included petroleum -8.7% and fertilisers -20.2%, opposed by office/ADP machines +7.3% and telecom equipment +4.1%. ABS attributes petroleum relief to improving supply during the quarter; this is not proof that current geopolitical threats are resolved. Lower import costs are a fresh offset to the inflation-path argument while export-price resilience supports external incomes. The export/import price ratio improved on these indexes; no national-accounts terms-of-trade actual or private inflow is asserted. Broker AU trade-price series were absent from the focused local snapshot; web calendar forecasts differ and are not treated as a unique consensus.

reviews.analysis: The Slight weakening call was aligned over its delivery-to-supersession diagnostic window, with all seven relative counterparts aligned. The saved rationale explicitly reduced the earlier grade after opposing private China PMI, domestic inflation and approvals evidence. This supports preserving an example of a narrow, opposed judgment that happened to align; it does not validate a universal hierarchy in which external demand always dominates domestic policy, nor establish an executable entry.
reviews.known_before_cutoff: The original call recorded positive private China PMI, hotter domestic inflation and approvals as material opposition to weak orders and official China contraction. Its grade was narrowed rather than simply carrying the old Moderate label.
reviews.subsequent_information: The next AUD assessment superseded this call at 06:35 UTC. This short outcome is not evidence of validity through the next day RBA package and does not include trading costs.
